body: Back to draft: the review found one blocker (A is not restated after the G30 tool change, so two ops at the same A can cut at the wrong index). The fix and its pinning test go on this branch, then flag it ready again for a re-review.

Fix for the review blocker (14314261): **A is now restated after every G30.**

- `assets/posts/tormach.cps`: `retract()` sets `aNow = null` right after it writes the bare `G30` (LinuxCNC moves every axis to the stored G30 position, params 5181-5189, A included). `endPreamble()` also forgets A, so every section opens with `G53 G0 Z0` / `G0 A..`. This covers the same-tool continuation too (no G30): a section boundary is where an operator may stop (M0/M1, a probe check) and jog, and the cost is one extra Z lift. The only G30s in the post are the tool-change one and the final one in `retract()`. There is no G28.
- **Pins** (`crates/app/tests/tormach_fourth_axis.rs`):
  - `a_tool_change_on_the_same_face_restates_a_after_the_g30`: two ops at A90, with T3 then T4. Both get `G53 G0 Z0` / `G0 A90` after their `M6`.
  - `a_same_tool_continuation_on_the_same_face_restates_a`: two ops at A90 with one tool. Both get the index.
  - Both pins **failed before the fix** (the second section had no `G0 A90`) and pass after it.
- **Goldens unchanged:** `index_4face_microarc4.nc` and the kit `microarc_test_part.nc` are byte-identical, because every op there indexes anyway.
- **Kit README** (`docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/README.md`):
  - New safety step: the safe Z is the top of travel, and the operator confirms that the part, chuck and jaws' swept radius clears the tool there before the first A move.
  - New safety step: every G30 can move A to the stored G30 A.
  - Checklist item 3: every op restates A after its M6.
  - Checklist item 7: A is now left at the G30 position's stored A, which is not necessarily 0.
- **Follow-up:** #804, "Tormach 4th axis: check the part/chuck swept radius against the safe Z before an A index".
- **Optional notes:**
  - `find_type`'s doc comment has moved back onto `find_type`.
  - New `crates/post/tests/mch_head_search.rs` tests the head search directly with a leaf ahead of the head. It fails against the old `?` search.
- **Decision** recorded in `docs/decisions/785-microarc-4th-axis.md`.

**Tests:**
- Local runs all pass: tormach_fourth_axis 12, microarc_test_part 2, conformance 6, tormach_post 10, tormach_safe_retract 4, machine 33, machine_library 11, post lib 7, mch_head_search 2.
- clippy `-p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.
- Linux quick gate (`--base upstream/main`) is green: post suites ok, app suites ok, 0 failed.

The PR stays a draft until it is re-readied.

Back to draft for one line: the tester-kit golden `docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/microarc_test_part.nc` isn't covered by `.gitattributes`' LF rule (only `crates/app/tests/golden/**` is), so on a Windows checkout it gets CRLF and `microarc_test_part::the_microarc_test_part_posts_its_indexed_program` fails on line endings alone. Found by @vilts while working #797 / PR #803. Adding `docs/tester-kits/**/*.nc text eol=lf`; it re-readies after a delta look.

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** Delta review 14314261..1045d2d7 (reviewed clean @ 14314261): one `.gitattributes` rule, `docs/tester-kits/**/*.nc text eol=lf`, the same treatment the goldens get. The kit program's blob is already LF (no CR in `microarc_test_part.nc`), so no renormalisation is needed and the byte-exact test now holds on a Windows checkout. No code change. MERGEABLE.
